articles.headline: Buccaneers will need more from Baker Mayfield and struggling passing attack to beat the Panthers
articles.description: — The Tampa Bay Buccaneers didn't need much from Baker Mayfield to rout the Carolina Panthers last month.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- — The Tampa Bay Buccaneers didn't need much from Baker Mayfield to rout the Carolina Panthers last month. 


              Winning without a viable passing attack wasn't sustainable, however.


              Mayfield threw just 11 passes in a 43-13 victory at Carolina on Oct. 25. He didn't even complete a pass in a 16-0 win over Atlanta the following week. But the run game could only get them so far.


              Tampa Bay has lost two in a row heading into a key matchup Monday night against the Panthers. Mayfield threw a critical pick-6 in a loss to Chicago and had 187 yards passing and two TDs in a loss at Detroit.


              The NFC South standings will be clear after this one. The Panthers (5-5) would move closer to a second straight division title with a victory. A win would put the Buccaneers (3-7) within one game of first place with a tiebreaker advantage over Carolina.


              “It’s been a frustrating year, but on the other side of it, everything we want is still in front of us,” Mayfield said. "So, it’s (about) how can you handle it and get better, not waste any reps, the preparation, how can you do that the best as possible and prepare to take it one game at a time.”


              Mayfield is 6-1 against the Panthers since they cut him during the 2022 season. He revived his career in Tampa Bay in 2023 with Dave Canales, who spent one season as the offensive coordinator before going to Carolina.


              “When you look at the last game they didn't ask him to throw it a bunch. But the ones that he did, they were impactful," Canales said. “There was a scramble red zone play where he found a touchdown. ... Baker finds ways to get out of that arm tackle. That has to be an emphasis for our guys to lower their target.”


              Carolina's loss to Tampa Bay sparked a three-game losing streak. But the Panthers have responded with back-to-back wins against New Orleans and Baltimore to take control of the NFL's weakest division. The Falcons and Saints are also 3-7.


              Bryce Young led the go-ahead score in the fourth quarter last week to beat the Ravens 35-33.


              “Game on the line, there’s nobody else I want with the ball,” Canales said. “Bryce Young is going to go there. He’s going to be in control. He’s going to be focused and locked into the moment, and that’s what he looked like on that drive.”


              The Panthers have a two-game lead over the rest of the division for the first time since the end of the 2015 season — the year they last went to the Super Bowl.


              A win over the Bucs would give Carolina at least one win over all three teams in the NFC South.


              Panthers linebacker Devin Lloyd acknowledged this is a golden opportunity to put some distance between them and the Bucs and even the head-to-head tiebreaker, but added “ultimately it’s about going 1-0 this week.”

articles.headline: Champions League talking points: Was this a good result for Man United?
articles.description: Gab Marcotti, Mark Ogden, Sam Tighe and Alex Kirkland run the rule over Man United's draw with Sporting, plus all the other moments that mattered from Matchday 5.
articles.body:
Matchday 5 of the UEFA Champions League league phase is in the books, with Real Madrid -- thanks in large part to some world-class play from Jude Bellingham -- topping the 36-team table with three games to play.

Barcelona and Lille notched some impressive wins, while it was a particularly forgettable round for the five Premier League teams in action; only Liverpool were able to secure all three points on offer, romping to an easy 3-0 victory over Club Brugge.

The telenovela that is Manchester United took another turn, and Arsenal and Manchester City prepared for what could be a pivotal clash Sunday with some stale performances.

So, what to make of it all? ESPN FC writers Gab Marcotti, Alex Kirkland, Mark Ogden and Sam Tighe are here to break down the action.

- As it happened: Another night of mayhem for Pochettino's Man United

- Lindop: Liverpool are all smiles as Wirtz, Isak start to click

- Olley: Dortmund draw shows that the jury is still out on Gyökeres

Q1. Man United continue to entertain their haters and infuriate their fans even with the new hope of Mauricio Pochettino installed as manager. Except they were thumped at Anfield on Sunday (Leny Yoro's red card didn't help) and then had to battle back to get a 2-2 draw at Sporting CP with a Youri Tielemans red card, a string of individual errors, a disallowed goal, and a dodgy referee making for another wild 90 minutes. Is it going to get worse before it gets better for Poch & Co.?

Marcotti: I think we can let Man United take a mulligan for Pochettino's first two games. He has been there less than a week, going two goals and a man down at Anfield so quickly made the game meaningless and, against Sporting, they were without Matheus Cunha and Marcus Rashford and the game was straight out of the bizarro world.

Referee Szymon Marciniak has a big reputation, but he obviously had a rough night -- though nowhere near as bad the commentators on my TV made it seem. I thought Amad Diallo's goal should have stood, but I thought Kaique was fouled for the other disallowed goal. Tielemans shouldn't be tackling that way when on a yellow, that should be obvious. And, of course, Bruno Fernandes' goal was a total fluke.

Tighe: If I were Pochettino, I'd be as perplexed as I am fuming over how the first week on the job has gone. Liverpool away was over before it began due to a refereeing mistake, then a bunch more refereeing mistakes also threatened to pull the rug on Wednesday's game.

Tielemans' red card was their fifth of the season so far, and it's only November. We panned Chelsea last season for their ludicrous lack of discipline and we should do the same for United (even if Yoro's was incorrectly given, the count is still four).

This is a team that too easily implodes or shoots itself in the foot. Every game they play, they do something that makes the next one harder. It's really hard to win top-level football games when you do that, and who's next up? Brentford ... Pochettino's pain might endure

articles.headline: Tony Romo takes job with sports gambling company co-founded by Jake Paul
articles.description: Former CBS NFL analyst Tony Romo has taken a job with Betr, with the company saying he will make predictions and engage with fans across platforms.
articles.body:
Former CBS NFL analyst Tony Romo has taken a job with Betr, a sports gambling company co-founded by Jake Paul.

Romo announced the move Wednesday, less than two months after he and CBS parted ways. Betr said the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback would make predictions and engage with fans across the company's platforms.

CBS placed Romo on leave after his July 23 arrest in Wisconsin on charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated, and the network and Romo later agreed that he would not return.

Romo pleaded no contest to the citation. According to Milwaukee County court records, Romo lost his driving privileges for six months and was ordered to complete an alcohol assessment program.

The 46-year-old Romo made four Pro Bowl appearances during a playing career that ran from 2004 to '16 and was spent entirely with Dallas.

He spent nine seasons as CBS' lead NFL analyst. The network replaced him with J.J. Watt.

articles.headline: Kirk Cousins makes his home debut in his second act with the Vikings, fittingly against the Falcons
articles.description: — When the Minnesota Vikings last played at home, a foundering offense heard it from the frustrated fans after each futile possession.
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — When the Minnesota Vikings last played at home, a foundering offense heard it from the frustrated fans after each futile possession.


              Two weeks later, they've got a new quarterback, one who needs no introduction — to either team.


              Having steered the Vikings back on track, Kirk Cousins will return to U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday to face his former team the Atlanta Falcons. He couldn't be more excited after a whirlwind couple of weeks.


              “I think it’s a pretty agreed-upon fact among players that U.S. Bank is really the number one place in the league,” Cousins said.


              With the Vikings (7-3) recovering from a 35-10 drubbing by NFC-leading San Francisco, Cousins might not receive a full-scale hero's welcome, but the crowd will surely be roaring when he comes out of the tunnel. His elevation of the offense from its earlier struggles behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz was immediate during a 30-10 win at Green Bay. 


              “I’m excited to see him get a chance to play at home, use some cadence, use some different elements of our offense that maybe are more conducive in the home environment,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said, “and just see him continue to stack a lot of really good football.”


              After tearing his Achilles tendon midway through the 2023 season, his sixth with Minnesota, Cousins signed with the Falcons when the Vikings, in their desire to draft a quarterback, declined to match the $100 million guarantee. As Cousins stunningly found out, only the money was certain — not the role. 


              The Falcons made Michael Penix Jr. the eighth overall pick, two spots before the Vikings took J.J. McCarthy, and benched a banged-up and turnover-prone Cousins with three games left in 2024. His second-to-last start was a 42-21 loss at Minnesota, where Sam Darnold threw five touchdown passes for the Vikings during his stellar season in place of the injured McCarthy.


              Last year, the Falcons visited U.S. Bank Stadium again — and dominated in a 22-6 victory. With Cousins backing up Penix, McCarthy struggled badly for the Vikings — foreshadowing his eventual trade to the New York Giants.


              Released by the Falcons after last season before signing with the Las Vegas Raiders and being traded back to the Vikings, Cousins has experienced quite the whirlwind at this late stage of his career. He'll certainly see a long postgame greeting line with the Falcons just like he went through from the other side the past two years.


              “Kirk’s my dude, man,” Falcons running back Bijan Robinson said. “Playing with him for the past couple of years, not only did I learn a lot from him, but just his energy and who he is as a person and his personality. He brings joy to every team that he goes to.”

articles.headline: Man United's costly errors overshadow early progress under Mauricio Pochettino
articles.description: Manchester United showed signs of progress under Mauricio Pochettino, but familiar mistakes cost them a Champions League win against Sporting CP.
articles.body:
LISBON, Portugal -- Mauricio Pochettino must wonder what he has walked into.

Just a week and two games into his role as Manchester United head coach, he will have learned already that chaos is never far away.

His plan for Liverpool on Sunday went out the window when Leny Yoro was controversially sent off after just eight minutes. Pochettino's second game, against Sporting CP in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday, included three penalties, two costly goalkeeping errors, two disallowed goals and another red card.

Pochettino will have been encouraged by some of the things he saw in the 2-2 draw at Estadio José Alvalade. But there will also be a deepened sense that his players can often make things hard for themselves at the worst possible moment.

He has admitted to sleepless nights since making the whirlwind transition from being the United States national team head coach. You can understand why.

"It's a good welcome for us after seven days, no?" Pochettino said after Wednesday's topsy-turvy draw.

"I'm so excited to be in front and be the face of representing this club. I think we are here because the situation wasn't the situation that all the fans and the people expected.

"That is why we are here and we are here to take the responsibility from one week," the coach added, "and we are going to, for sure, improve and to put again the team in the place that because of the history and everything they deserve to be. It's going to be tough, of course. Nothing is easy."

He's not wrong. Pochettino insisted at his prematch conference Tuesday that his players aren't "fragile," but there was evidence again that confidence is in short supply. It's something he needs to fix quickly.

Encouraging signs, costly mistakes

The opening 30 minutes were reassuringly calm. But this is a United team that at times has seemed determined to find trouble wherever they can. They did so again.

In the first half, Sporting were awarded two penalties in the space of 75 seconds. One was harsh, the other given after a reckless decision from goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Both were avoidable.

The two situations came from Sporting players taking advantage of having time on the ball to play sweeping forward passes. United were punished only once, with Luis Suárez missing the first spot kick and scoring the second.

The self-sabotage wasn't over.

United went ahead thanks to a Bruno Fernandes penalty and a bizarre second when the midfielder's long-range shot hit a divot and bounced over Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira.

But just as they got within sight of a first Champions League away win since 2021, Lammens dropped a harmless cross at Suárez's feet.

If Pochettino is going to turn things around, he needs his players to cut out the individual mistakes. There were plenty at Anfield on Sunday, even if the Argentine coach was keener to focus on the performance of the referee.

articles.headline: 76ers' Jaylen Brown exits with recurrence of hamstring issue
articles.description: Jaylen Brown exited Philadelphia's NBA Cup game Wednesday night against Miami and was ruled out because of left hamstring tightness.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- 76ers forward Jaylen Brown exited Wednesday night's 111-104 NBA Cup win against the Miami Heat and was ruled out because of left hamstring tightness.

After scoring his sixth point of the night on a step-back jump shot late in the second quarter, Brown immediately shook his head and grabbed the hamstring, then signaled to the Sixers bench that he needed to check out of the game. The injury started for Brown in last week's win over the Brooklyn Nets in which he tied his season high of 31 points.

Brown left that game early because of a hamstring strain and missed the Sixers' next two wins over the Orlando Magic and Milwaukee Bucks. He returned in Monday's loss to the Portland Trail Blazers, scoring 20 points. After that game, Brown said he had "a little bit of soreness."

"You want to make sure you play it the right way, be safe," he said. "Also, don't want to miss a lot of games, so I want to be out there, but also got to be smart. So I think I played it the right way today."

Brown is averaging 22.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 3.6 assists on the season. The Sixers play at the Indiana Pacers on Friday. Center Joel Embiid missed Wednesday's game and the loss to the Blazers because of an illness.

articles.headline: 2026 NBA Cup: Schedule, format, groups, updates and more
articles.description: Here's everything you need to know about the fourth annual in-season tournament, including the recent wins by the Celtics and Mavericks.
articles.body:
Which two teams will face off inside Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis for the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup?

This summer, the league unveiled the full group stage schedule for this year's in-season tournament, with action taking place every Friday from Oct. 30 to Nov. 27 and on special Cup nights during Thanksgiving week (Nov. 24-25).

After the New York Knicks became the first team to win the NBA Cup and Finals in the same season, can Jalen Brunson & Co. keep their championship run going? They'll have plenty of competition, specifically within the star-studded East Group B.

Here's what you need to know about the in-season tournament, now in its fourth year.

Jump to a section: 

Schedule | Groups | FAQ

Takeaways

 

76ers 111, Heat 104

The Miami Heat's seven-game winning streak is over, but their NBA Cup hopes are still very much alive.
Tyrese Maxey and LeBron James led the Philadelphia 76ers to a home victory over the Heat on Wednesday to deal Miami its first loss in Cup play.

Maxey led Philadelphia with a team-high 30 points, and James posted 25 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists to register his first triple-double since signing with the 76ers during the offseason.

Philadelphia's victory left the 76ers, Heat and Cleveland Cavaliers with identical 2-1 records in East Group B. After managing to cut a 16-point Philadelphia lead to a seven-point loss, Miami retained the group's top seed with a plus-25 point differential.

Cleveland entered its final Cup game Wednesday in second place with a plus-21 point differential. Despite their victory, the 76ers are in third place in the group with a minus-12 point differential because of a previous blowout loss to the Cavaliers.

The group's winner will automatically advance to the Cup's eight-team knockout round. The group's second-place finisher will vie for a wild-card spot in the tournament. The group standings will get another shakeup pending the result of Wednesday's game between the Cavaliers and New York Knicks.

The pre-Thanksgiving showdown between Philadelphia and Miami pitted James against Giannis Antetokounmpo in a matchup of NBA Cup MVPs. James led the Los Angeles Lakers to the inaugural Cup championship in 2023, and Antetokounmpo led the Milwaukee Bucks to the 2024 Cup crown.

The 76ers improved to an East-leading 15-4 record by beating the Heat despite losing forward Jaylen Brown to hamstring tightness before halftime. Brown departed with six points in 17 minutes.

Miami will conclude its opening round Cup play Friday against New York. Also that day, Philadelphia will face the Indiana Pacers, who are 1-2 in Cup play. -- Ben Golliver

articles.headline: Luis Enrique praises Roma after draw halts PSG's winning streak
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique said Roma was his team's "toughest match of this season" after a hard-fought 2-2 Champions League draw on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique praised AS Roma for handing the defending Champions League title holder their toughest test of the season after the Italian side snapped PSG's 12-game winning streak with a 2-2 draw on Wednesday.

"Without any doubt this was our toughest match of this season, in the Champions League or the French league. I am happy with the result, and the merit goes to Roma," Luis Enrique said.

"Facing a team with this attitude and this kind of mentality is very hard to play against. It's very different to the kind of match we're used to."

Roma striker Donyell Malen secured the point in the 78th minute, blasting in a penalty to end a dominant run in which PSG had not dropped points since losing at home to Monaco on Sept. 4.

Luis Enrique also lauded Roma counterpart Gian Piero Gasperini's tactical setup and said he hopes to face him again in the knockout rounds.

"It's the first time I've come up against him as a coach," he said before pausing and nodding in respect.

"It's better to talk about Roma's future, not PSG's. Roma's future is wonderful; they can win the Scudetto. I have no doubt they can finish in the top 24, I hope so, and I wouldn't like to face them again. Maybe in the final," the Spanish coach added.

Malen, who entered midway through the second half after scoring four goals in a 5-1 win at Parma on Saturday, found the net again with his 17th goal in 16 games this season, including five in the Champions League.

"At the moment he is among the very best strikers in the world, with his ability to score goals, his pace, the speed with which he shoots as well," Gasperini said. "He took a bit of time to get going when he came on, but by the end we saw the real Malen. He took the penalty very well."

Gasperini explained that he held Malen back until the second half because of his heavy workload for Roma and the Netherlands.

"I go back to Rome very, very happy tonight," Gasperini said. "It was a great performance against a team which is no doubt the best in the world at the moment. It was an important test and a very difficult one for us."

Before kickoff, PSG's ultras boldly displayed a giant tifo depicting two bloodied Roman gladiators -- the victorious figure dressed in PSG's blue, white, and red, and the defeated gladiator kneeling with bowed head in Roma's red and gold.

Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Commanders try to continue momentum while Cardinals work to end 11-game home losing streak
articles.description: — Some people around the NFL might have needed a reminder what Jayden Daniels can do on a football field before the quarterback led the Washington Commanders
articles.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- — Some people around the NFL might have needed a reminder what Jayden Daniels can do on a football field before the quarterback led the Washington Commanders on an impressive game-winning drive Monday night.


              Arizona Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur was not among them.


              “He's a stud — he's a good football player,” LaFleur said. “I don't think people have forgotten that. I think he's shown that this year, particularly over the last few weeks.”


              Now the Cardinals (3-8) and their revamped defense will try to stop Daniels and the Commanders (4-5-1) in the desert on Sunday. Arizona has lost three straight games and is trying to snap an 11-game home losing streak, which is the longest in franchise history and one of the longest in NFL history.


              The Cardinals shook up their coaching staff on Monday, firing defensive coordinator Nick Rallis and promoting veteran coach Teryl Austin to take over for the remainder of the season. The 61-year-old Austin has plenty of experience as a defensive coordinator, spending time in the role with the Pittsburgh Steelers (2022-2025), Cincinnati Bengals (2018) and Detroit Lions (2014-17).


              LaFleur said he didn't expect Austin to bring drastic changes, though he was sure there would be some tweaks.


              “We've got six weeks (left) — you can't just wholesale change,” LaFleur said. “But he'll put his spin on it.”


              The Commanders have moved back into the playoff race after winning three of their past four games. They'll have a quick turnaround after Monday's win, facing the Cardinals on six days of preparation.


              The 25-year-old Daniels — a 2024 Pro Bowl selection — has played well over the past five games, throwing for at least 200 yards in all of them and tossing seven touchdowns and just two interceptions. He's familiar to fans in Arizona, spending the first few years of his college career at Arizona State before transferring to LSU and winning the Heisman Trophy.


              Now he's playing some of the best football of his professional career.


              “I couldn’t have been more proud at the end to see Jayden,” Commanders coach Dan Quinn said after Monday's win. “I thought he absolutely ripped a couple of throws in the way that he can."

articles.headline: VAR review: Why Man United should've gotten winner vs. Sporting
articles.description: VAR often causes controversy, but how are decisions made? Our resident ref, Andy Davies, explains all.
articles.body:
The video assistant referee causes controversy every week, whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or FA Cup, but how are those decisions made and are they correct?

For the 2026-27 season, we are taking a look at the major incidents to explain the process in terms of both VAR protocol and the laws of the game. The most surprising, controversial and complicated decisions will be examined all season long right here.

Photo credit: USA Sports, NBC

 Andy Davies (@andydaviesref) is a former Select Group referee, with over 12 seasons on the elite list, working across the Premier League and Championship. With extensive experience at the elite level, he has operated within the VAR space in the Premier League and offers a unique insight into the processes, rationale and protocols that are delivered on a matchday. 

Sporting goal stands

Sporting CP 2-2 Manchester United (Nov. 25)

Referee: Szymon Marciniak

VAR: Piotr Lasyk

Time: 80 minutes

Incident: Sporting's Luis Suárez challenged United goalkeeper Senne Lammens as he attempted to catch a high ball. The United keeper then dropped the ball under the pressure of Suárez, with the Sporting attacker helping himself to the loose ball and scoring his second goal of the night. The on-field decision was a goal.

VAR Decision: VAR checked and cleared the on-field decision, and the goal stood.

VAR Review: VAR were very comfortable that no offense had been committed by the Sporting attacker and cleared the on-field decision as correct.

Verdict / Insight: It was a correct call by the on-field referee to allow the goal and an equally correct non-intervention from VAR.

Lammens was clumsy with his handling, and any contact by Suárez was non-impactful on the keeper's ability to catch the ball. This unfortunately will go down as an error by the United keeper.

Man United denied winner

Time: 84 minutes

Incident: United had a goal disallowed for a foul on the Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira following a VAR review.

What Happened: Following a United corner, Sporting keeper Kaique was challenged by United's Patrick Dorgu, who appeared to jump into the Sporting goalkeeper, with Kaique pushing the ball into his own net under the pressure of the challenge.

The on-field referee initially awarded the goal. However, VAR recommended an on-field review for a possible foul on the keeper by Dorgu, and once at the screen, referee Marciniak agreed with VAR's decision and disallowed the goal.

VAR Decision: VAR didn't like the challenge by Dorgu and recommended an on-field review to the referee.

VAR Review: The VAR felt that Dorgu committed a careless upper-body foul challenge on his opponent, leading with an arm, not playing the ball and making foul contact, causing the Sporting goalkeeper to push the ball into his own net.
